Stop an open, and say why, when the saved projects can't be read

Opening a file asks whether it was opened before by listing the projects
folder. With that folder unreadable, the Agent's project_open crashed
JusPrin with an uncaught "directory_iterator: Access is denied"
(reproduced in the app). A person's File > Open goes through the same
lookup.

The listing now reports an unreadable projects folder as a result, not
an exception. One helper lists the project folders with the error_code
forms. projects() and projects_for_source() return nothing in that case,
meaning "unknown", which is not the same as "no projects" or "not opened
before". Each caller decides what that means:

- Opening a file stops before anything is replaced, because the
  question can't be answered and a project made from the file couldn't
  be saved either. A person sees "Your saved projects couldn't be read
  ... The file wasn't opened." The Agent's project_open fails with
  local_save_failed (the listed code whose next step, tell the person,
  fits), whether at the request or at its run. ToolExecutionCoordinator's
  lookup callback gains an EarlierLookup with an unreadable flag; a
  callback returning just the optional project still converts to it.
- Home says the projects couldn't be loaded, as before, now without the
  catch added for it.
- The header's Recent projects menu says "Projects couldn't be loaded".

--unavailable-storage checks both opens with the projects folder locked:
nothing opens, the reason is given, and the current project stays. A
coordinator unit test covers the unreadable answer at request and at
run.

The last item is fixed and committed to `claude/autosave-unwritable` as `19cd8379bd`, on top of `122da1df30`, `4180969b01` and `fe6175df41`. Nothing is pushed.

**What was wrong.** With the projects folder unreadable, the Agent's `project_open` crashed JusPrin. The error was the same uncaught "directory_iterator … Access is denied"; I reproduced it in the app first. A person's File > Open goes through the same "have you opened this file before?" lookup.

**What I changed.** Listing the projects folder now reports "couldn't read the folder" as an ordinary answer instead of throwing. That answer means "unknown", which is different from "no projects" or "not opened before". Each caller decides what "unknown" means:
- **Opening a file stops before anything is replaced.** The question can't be answered, and a new project couldn't be saved anyway. A person sees: "Your saved projects couldn't be read, so JusPrin can't check whether you've opened this file before. The file wasn't opened. Try again once JusPrin can read its projects folder." The Agent's call fails with `local_save_failed` and a message saying exactly that. I reused that existing code because the code list says to reuse the one whose next step fits, and here that's "tell the person".
- **Home** still says the projects couldn't be loaded. It no longer needs the special error handling I added for it earlier.
- **The header's Recent projects menu** says "Projects couldn't be loaded. Try again."

**Checked in the app** (same steps as the crash):
- The Agent's open now returns that message and the app stays up.
- A person's Ctrl+O on a 3MF shows the "Couldn't open file" dialog and the current project stays open.
- After access returned, the title went back to "Saved" and the same open worked.

**Tests.**
- `--unavailable-storage` now covers both kinds of open (all checks pass), and a coordinator unit test covers the "couldn't tell" answer.
- All the related harness modes pass, including `reopen-prompt`, and the workspace harness passes all 5,976 checks.
- The default mode's 8 failures are all among the 14 the unfixed build also fails.
- One Agent unit test fails (an attachment-preview test that expects `\n` but gets `\r\n`, a Windows line-ending fixture). I didn't touch it, and I didn't run it on the unfixed build.

**Sweep of everything that reads the projects folder:**

| Place | Status |
|---|---|
| Project list (Home, Recent projects menu) | Fixed (previous commit) |
| "Opened before?" lookup (person and Agent opens) | Fixed (this commit) |
| Resuming the last project at startup | Already handled: the failure is caught and reported, and the app starts on a blank project; Home, shown at startup, now explains the problem |
| Version store and autosave | Already handled: reported as "Couldn't save" and retried |
| Opening a saved project, and restoring a version | Already handled, with a dialog |
| Attachment reads | Already handled: they return a failure result |
| Importing JusPrin state from an older-style 3MF | Not fixed. It writes into the project folder only during an open, which now stops first. If the folder became unreadable in the moment between the check and the load, that path could still throw. |
| Preferences "Show versions folder" | Nothing to fix: it only opens the folder in Explorer |

do you keep the project content in memory now? if so, what did you do to make sure it's not out of sync with the file on disk?

No. Only the **list of saved versions** is kept in memory: for each version its id, time, project name, the file it came from, and which object files it uses. The project content stays on disk and is read from disk whenever it's needed. That includes the model geometry, the settings in each version and the current conversation document, so restoring a version still reads and checks the real files.

**Why the list can't drift from disk during normal use:**
- **A saved version is never changed after it's written.** No code edits or rewrites a committed version, so there's nothing to re-read.
- **Only one writer per project.** Each open project holds an operating-system file lock, and a second JusPrin instance is refused; the harness tests that. Nothing else in JusPrin writes those files.
- **Memory changes only after the disk change succeeds**, at the same three moments the on-disk index (`HEAD`) changes:
  - when the project opens, every version is read from disk;
  - after a save, once `HEAD` is written, the new entry is added by parsing the exact text just written to disk, not copied from the in-memory version;
  - after old versions are cleaned up, once `HEAD` is rewritten, the list is trimmed to match.

  If a disk write fails, the in-memory list is left as it was.
- **It follows how the store already worked.** It already kept the current version, the committed-version index and the last saved state in memory. The version list was the one piece re-read from disk on every call.

**What it does not catch:**
- **Changes from outside JusPrin.** If someone deletes a version folder by hand, or a sync tool or antivirus removes one while the project is open, the list keeps showing that version until the project is reopened. Before my change, a version whose files had disappeared silently dropped out of the list. Now it stays listed, and choosing it fails visibly, because restore reads and validates the real files. I didn't mention this behaviour change in my earlier reports, and should have.
- **No test compares the in-memory list with disk after a long run of saves and cleanups.** The existing tests check reopening and that history survives cleanup, but none checks the two match step by step. I can add one to the workspace harness if you'd like.

input.content:
Keep JusPrin up and visible when the projects folder can't be read or written

When a project's folder, or the whole projects folder, stopped being
readable, JusPrin crashed. The cases were an Agent page refresh, opening
Home, and opening a file (the "opened this file before?" lookup). On
Windows, denying "write" with icacls also blocks reading, which is how
the Preferences restart test hit it.

Version list. The Agent page builds its restore points from the version
list, and ProjectVersionStore::history() re-read every manifest.json on
each page refresh. Committed manifests never change, and the store is
their only writer, guarded by an OS file lock. So history() now returns
a list read once when the project opens. publish() extends it, from the
exact manifest text written, after HEAD is replaced. prune() trims it
after HEAD is rewritten. Saves still fail and are reported as "Couldn't
save" while autosave retries. A version deleted from outside JusPrin
stays listed until the project is reopened, and restoring it fails
visibly. pin_current() reports a failed pin as a failed save instead of
throwing past the chat checkpoint.

Projects folder. Listing it now reports "can't be read" as a result, not
an exception. One helper uses the error_code forms. projects() and
projects_for_source() return nothing for "unknown", and each caller
decides what that means:
- Home says "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
  instead of "No projects yet." While that is shown, HomeHost's
  once-a-second live refresh re-reads the folder, so the gallery fills
  in by itself; Home has no back button to reopen it.
- The header's Recent projects menu says the projects couldn't be loaded.
- Opening a file stops before anything is replaced, since whether it was
  opened before can't be told. A person is told so. The Agent's
  project_open fails with local_save_failed, at the request or at its
  run, through a new EarlierLookup answer from the coordinator's lookup
  callback.
- One project folder that can't be read is left out of the lists like
  any damaged project. Its HEAD check was outside the per-project
  handling, and on POSIX exists() throws for a folder without permission.

Tests. The new shell-harness mode --unavailable-storage takes away
access to the open project's folder, then to the whole projects folder.
It uses the folder's ACL on Windows, where POSIX mode bits are not
enforced, and checks every case above recovers by itself once access
returns. The unfixed build fails it with the original error. New
jusprin_tests and agent_bridge_tests cases cover the Home payload and
retry, and the coordinator's unreadable answer.

Two Windows-only test failures are fixed on the way:
- home_describes_managed_project looked for "/jusprin/projects/" in a
  native path that uses backslashes on Windows. It now compares folders.
- slice_failure_in_orca_words expected the English catalogue's wording
  of the bed-type refusal. Windows shows the source text, and neither
  wording has changed upstream. It now builds the expected text through
  _u8L, as Plater does.
